correctness.rationale: The forbidden ordered child-root pair removes exactly one quadratic monomial from the appropriate root-specific count, giving the three recurrences for every height. All admissible finite blocks extend. Rational invariant intervals and strict derivative bounds imply unique ratio-map fixed points with geometric attraction. Telescoping gives a positive absolutely convergent hidden-entropy series with explicit tail bound; an exact chain of squared-proportion inequalities establishes strict ordering across all heights. The series tail plus contraction yields the prefactor and the specified exponential error. Exact brute force up to height four and rational endpoint tests corroborate the analytic identities but are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: A natural complete eight-pattern one-star census gives three distinct hidden growth constants with a strict order and a sharp finite-height multiplicative asymptotic. Ban and Chang already introduced the general nonlinear counting method and coarser log-two entropy for the binary case and explicitly identified its hidden entropy as an open computation problem; those are not claimed as new. The inspected relevant sections of the most plausible primary papers and comparable published claims did not state the combined classification, strict inequality and prefactors. Historical coverage is necessarily limited and independently unvalidated.
residual_risks: The count recurrence is a specialization of established two-symbol tree-shift nonlinear recursion theory; the novelty assessment concerns its complete three-class analytical evaluation, not the recurrence principle.
A general numerical ratio-map analysis or an unindexed table could implicitly yield some or all of the special-case constants without using the same terminology.
Aubrun–Béal (2012) was checked only through its abstract; no whole-text non-coverage claim is drawn.
Historical priority and significance have not been independently audited.

value.rationale: Hidden entropy is an explicitly motivated quantitative invariant of tree shifts, not determined by the coarse entropy log two. The smallest natural class of nontrivial binary Markov restrictions with exactly one forbidden parent/left/right-child star consists of precisely eight cases and admits a complete strict three-class comparison. The proof determines effective constants, first distinguishing finite counts, fixed-point root biases and the exact asymptotic prefactor, all useful for estimating finite-tree languages and demonstrating that equal coarse entropy conceals quantifiable complexity differences. This is a complete motivated classification, not an arbitrary computational slice.
